name: American English (General American)

ancestors.notes: Middle English descent via colonial English

notes: General American (GA) — reference accent for US media/education. RHOTIC: /r/ preserved in all positions. No TRAP-BATH split (bath words = /æ/). LOT-PALM merger: /ɑ/ for both (written without the length mark — see BROAD BY DECLARATION and the no-length-marks paragraph below). T-FLAPPING: /t/ → [ɾ] between vowels (butter, water, city) — an ALLOPHONIC process, declared in `allophones` and deliberately not in the default broad output; see BROAD BY DECLARATION below. Source: Wells (1982) vol. 3, Ladefoged & Johnson (2011). FLAPPING: /t/ and /d/ → [ɾ] intervocalically in unstressed syllables (butter, ladder, city). RHOTIC: fully rhotic — /r/ preserved in all positions. GA GOAT is /oʊ/, not the RP /əʊ/ this spec's parent declares (Wells 1982 vol.3 §6.1.4). The RP coda-/r/ deletion this spec inherits is re-declared with no target phonemes (Wells 1982 vol.3 §6.1; Ladefoged & Johnson 2011) — the id-keyed way a dialect states it lacks a parent's process. SUFFIX PALATALIZATION, RHOTIC COLUMN: the three yod-coalescing suffixes this spec inherits end in a coda /r/ that GA keeps, so each is re-declared with the r-coloured schwa [ɚ] in place of the RP [ə]. ENDING "ture" is [tʃɚ] (nature, picture, feature) — the coalesced coronal plus GA r-coloured schwa (Wells 2008 LPD; Wells 1982 vol 3 §6.1). ENDING "sure" is [ʒɚ] (measure, closure, leisure) — the same, with the voiced coronal (Wells 2008 LPD; Wells 1982 vol 3 §6.1). ENDING "ssure" is [ʃɚ] (pressure, fissure) — the same after the voiceless ⟨ss⟩, which longest-match-wins picks over ⟨-sure⟩ (Wells 2008 LPD; Wells 1982 vol 3 §6.1). BROAD BY DECLARATION: the default transcription is PHONEMIC. T/D-FLAPPING and word-initial aspiration are sub-phonemic realisations of /t/ and /d/ (Wells 1982 vol.3 §6.1.5 on the GA tapped /t/; Kretzschmar 2004 §2, which describes flapping as an allophonic rule of the reference accent; Ladefoged & Johnson 2011 ch. 3 on English aspiration as an allophone of the voiceless stop series), so they are declared in `allophones` — the field that states a phoneme's surface variants — and NOT forced into the default output by `positional_graphemes`. The narrow-vs-broad choice is the data's to make (see orthography2ipa.inventory.phoneme_inventory), and GA reference sources transcribe /t/ and /d/ phonemically (Kenyon & Knott 1953; Labov, Ash & Boberg 2006). General American is conventionally transcribed WITHOUT length marks: the RP length contrast this spec's parent declares is not part of the GA system, where the tense/lax opposition carries the contrast and duration is its allophonic correlate (Wells 1982 vol.3 §6.1.1; Kenyon & Knott 1953, the reference American pronouncing dictionary, which uses no length mark at all; Labov, Ash & Boberg 2006 §2.1, whose North-American vowel system is stated the same way; Kretzschmar 2004 §2). General American has TRUE r-coloured vowels, written with the rhotacised symbols ɝ (stressed NURSE) and ɚ (unstressed lettER) rather than as a vowel plus a separate rhotic consonant (Wells 1982 vol.3 §6.1.2; Kenyon & Knott 1953; Ladefoged & Johnson 2011 ch. 4; Kretzschmar 2004 §2). NO-LENGTH COVERAGE: the length marks are dropped by per-phoneme rules, so every length-bearing emission needs one. Besides the plain vowels that means the yod-plus-GOOSE compound ⟨u⟩/⟨eau⟩ reads as (juː → ju), and the five strong-form function words the parent freezes whole in `word_exceptions` (be, he, me, we, she) — a frozen exception bypasses the rule layer by design, so those are restated here in American notation rather than rewritten (Kenyon & Knott 1953; Wells 2008 LPD). The variant sets in `allophones` still list ʉː and ɝː, which is correct: those are declared VARIANTS of the parent's vowels and never the default reading. GRAPHEME ⟨aa⟩: the digraph occurs in English only in loans and proper names (aardvark, bazaar, salaam, Aachen), where GA reads it as the single low back vowel ɑ, never as a vowel sequence (Wells 2008 LPD). Without the entry the two ⟨a⟩s are read separately and the word gains a spurious syllable.

location.notes: the geographic centre of the United States. General American is a media/education reference accent with NO regional home at all — this is the weakest point in the dataset and should be read as such. [Wikidata Q30 P625]

allophone_rules.notes: LOT-PALM merger: GA has no /ɒ/ - the RP LOT vowel merges with PALM as unrounded /ɑ/ (Wells 1982 vol.3 6.1.3).

General American is fully rhotic: /r/ is preserved in every position, so the RP coda-/r/ deletion this spec inherits does not apply (Wells 1982 vol.3 §6.1; Ladefoged & Johnson 2011). Declared with no target phonemes, the id-keyed way a dialect states it lacks a parent's process.

R-COLOURED VOWELS (see notes): stressed NURSE is the single r-coloured vowel ɝ in GA, not a vowel plus a separate rhotic — bird, nurse, herd, word (Wells 1982 vol.3 §6.1.2; Kenyon & Knott 1953; Ladefoged & Johnson 2011 ch. 4; Kretzschmar 2004 §2). KNOWN LIMIT: the rewrite is per-emission, so a word that reaches the r-coloured vowel from one slot and a separate ⟨r⟩ grapheme from the next still surfaces as ɝɹ (and, less often, ɚɹ) — a vowel plus a separate rhotic, which is exactly what the r-coloured symbol is supposed to replace. Measured on the ipadict en-US gold this affects a small minority of words. Collapsing it needs a cross-slot condition the rule vocabulary does not express, so it is recorded here rather than papered over.

R-COLOURED VOWELS (see notes): unstressed lettER is ɚ, the same vowel as ɝ without the accent — doctor, dollar, standard (Wells 1982 vol.3 §6.1.2; Kenyon & Knott 1953; Ladefoged & Johnson 2011 ch. 4). KNOWN LIMIT: the rule keys on the parent's ə+rhotic reading, so an ⟨-er⟩ word whose ⟨er⟩ the weights resolve to the NURSE reading instead (letter) surfaces with ɝ. Conditioning on stress=unstressed is the correct phonology and fixes those words, but measured PER-NEGATIVE on the one gold that has the distinction (ipadict en-US 0.3549 → 0.3652), which writes ɝ unstressed too.
NO LENGTH MARKS (see notes): START — car, park, hard — is plain ɑ before the rhotic GA keeps (Wells 1982 vol.3 §6.1.1; Kenyon & Knott 1953; Labov, Ash & Boberg 2006 §2.1).
NO LENGTH MARKS (see notes): NORTH/FORCE — more, born, four — is plain ɔ before the rhotic (Wells 1982 vol.3 §6.1.1; Kenyon & Knott 1953; Labov, Ash & Boberg 2006 §2.1).
NO LENGTH MARKS (see notes): PALM/LOT, the merged low back vowel EN_US_LOT_PALM_MERGER already states, written ɑ (Wells 1982 vol.3 §6.1.1; Kenyon & Knott 1953; Labov, Ash & Boberg 2006 §2.1).

NO LENGTH MARKS (see notes): THOUGHT/CLOTH, written ɔ (Wells 1982 vol.3 §6.1.1; Kenyon & Knott 1953). KEPT DISTINCT from PALM: Labov, Ash & Boberg 2006 ch. 9 map the cot-caught merger as an in-progress REGIONAL change, not as the GA reference system this spec models, so the merger is deliberately not declared.

NO LENGTH MARKS (see notes): FLEECE, written i (Wells 1982 vol.3 §6.1.1; Kenyon & Knott 1953; Labov, Ash & Boberg 2006 §2.1). This also delivers GA happY tensing — city, happy, coffee — since the parent already reads final ⟨y⟩ as the FLEECE vowel (Wells 1982 §2.2.24; GA is tense).
NO LENGTH MARKS (see notes): GOOSE, written u (Wells 1982 vol.3 §6.1.1; Kenyon & Knott 1953; Labov, Ash & Boberg 2006 §2.1).

NO LENGTH MARKS (see notes): the yod-plus-GOOSE compound that ⟨u⟩ and ⟨eau⟩ read as — cue, value, accrue, beauty. It is ONE declared emission, so segmentation matches it whole and the plain uː rule never sees it; without this entry the accent's own no-length invariant leaks on every yod word (Wells 1982 vol.3 §6.1.1; Kenyon & Knott 1953).
R-COLOURED VOWELS (see notes): any residual bare ɜː is ɝ — the parent's NURSE vowel does not occur without rhoticity in a rhotic accent (Wells 1982 vol.3 §6.1.2; Kenyon & Knott 1953).

Same ⟨-oing⟩ hiatus as the parent, on this spec's own GOAT vowel: the parent states the RP [əʊ], and General American has [oʊ] — the value this spec's ⟨o⟩ grapheme already declares. Re-declared rather than inherited because the surface of an allophone rule is a literal, so a diphthong written into a parent rule cannot follow a child's inventory on its own.
